text:
Connor Dewar is Pittsburgh's energy centre: about 13:38 a night, penalty killing, dump-ins and forechecking. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he carries the puck in on only 23% of his entries, so his line lives on the forecheck. Two goals and five points in 18 games is about what that job pays.

The interesting part is that his line has been good. With Dewar on the ice at five on five, the Penguins have taken 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), seven points better than when he sits. On a team sitting near the bottom of the standings, that's a depth player doing his job. Evolving-Hockey liked his 2025-26 a lot (2.2 wins above replacement, 42nd among forwards) but warns that his results ran ahead of his chances, about double what the chances said, so don't expect a repeat of that number. He also draws more penalties than he takes. If Pittsburgh does start selling veterans, a cheap, useful fourth-line centre is the kind of player contenders call about.
